title: Upper Atbara and Setit dams: Gulf and Arab funds, tens of thousands moved

lenders.name: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development
lenders.role: Loans 557/2010, 566/2011 and a supplementary KD 30 million loan; together about 22% of the KD 512.6 million cost (Arab Fund).

lenders.name: Kuwait Fund, Saudi Fund for Development, Islamic Development Bank, OPEC Fund, Government of Algeria
lenders.role: Together about KD 175 million, roughly 34% of the cost (Arab Fund). The OPEC Fund share was US$30 million, signed 24 February 2012 (OPEC Fund).

lenders.name: Government of China
lenders.role: About KD 29.2 million, about 7% of the cost at the time of the first Arab Fund loan (Arab Fund); listed as co-financier by the OPEC Fund.

lenders.name: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD)
lenders.role: US$90 million concessionary loan that it says contributed to completing the Rumela and Burdana dams feeding the 320 MW plant (ADFD, February 2017).

conditions: Two connected dams and a 320 MW plant. The Arab Fund's project page includes land acquisition, property compensation and resettlement of about 138,000 inhabitants. The Arab Fund's project page says its loan "covers about 11% of the total project cost" and lists land expropriation and resettlement as one of the parts it pays for, including buying land, compensating property owners and the "resettlement of 138 thousand inhabitants affected by the construction of the project". The loan was KD 50.0 million at 2.5% interest, with a 7-year grace period, a 25-year maturity and repayment in 37 half-yearly instalments. The page sets out no other conditions (Arab Fund).

title: EU and Italian Money for Libya's Coast Guard and Migrant Detention

lenders.name: European Union (grant)
